title: Smallest Range Covering Elements from K Lists
description: Find the smallest range [a, b] that includes at least one number from each of the k lists.
pseudocode:
1. Initialize min-heap with the first element of each list.
2. Track max value in heap and current range.
3. While all lists have elements:
4. Extract min, update range if smaller.
5. If min element list has more, push next to heap and update max.
6. Else, break loop.

steps.note: Initialize heap with heads: [0 (list 1), 4 (list 0), 5 (list 2)]. Max is 5.
Pop 0 (list 1). Range [0, 5]. Add 9 from list 1. Heap: [4, 5, 9]. Max is 9.
Pop 4 (list 0). Range [4, 9]. Add 10 from list 0. Heap: [5, 9, 10]. Max is 10.
Pop 5 (list 2). Range [5, 10]. Add 18 from list 2. Heap: [9, 10, 18]. Max is 18.
Pop 9 (list 1). Range [9, 18]. Add 12 from list 1. Heap: [10, 12, 18]. Max is 18.
Pop 10 (list 0). Range [10, 18]. Add 15 from list 0. Heap: [12, 15, 18]. Max is 18.
Pop 12 (list 1). Range [12, 18]. Add 20 from list 1. Heap: [15, 18, 20]. Max is 20.
Pop 15 (list 0). Range [15, 20]. Add 24 from list 0. Heap: [18, 20, 24]. Max is 24.
Pop 18 (list 2). Range [18, 24]. Add 22 from list 2. Heap: [20, 22, 24]. Max is 24.

fullDescription:
You have k lists of sorted integers in non-decreasing order. Find the smallest range that includes at least one number from each of the k lists.

We define the range [a, b] is smaller than range [c, d] if b - a < d - c or a < c if b - a == d - c.

 

Example 1:

Input: nums = [[4,10,15,24,26],[0,9,12,20],[5,18,22,30]]
Output: [20,24]
Explanation: 
List 1: [4, 10, 15, 24,26], 24 is in range [20,24].
List 2: [0, 9, 12, 20], 20 is in range [20,24].
List 3: [5, 18, 22, 30], 22 is in range [20,24].

Example 2:

Input: nums = [[1,2,3],[1,2,3],[1,2,3]]
Output: [1,1]

 

Constraints:

  • nums.length == k
  • 1 <= k <= 3500
  • 1 <= nums[i].length <= 50
  • -105 <= nums[i][j] <= 105
  • nums[i] is sorted in non-decreasing order.
